incidents.victim: French and European supermarkets, a blood supply service, and small hydroelectric facilities
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised internet-exposed refrigeration controllers and Schneider Electric industrial equipment, likely via vulnerable firmware or default credentials, to remotely override temperature settings.
incidents.impact: Two waves of attacks (Oct 11-12 and Nov 1-2) spoiled food at roughly 700-800 French and European supermarkets and caused at least 15 fires; France's blood transfusion service and small hydroelectric plants were also hit, and French authorities formally attributed the campaign to the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit (CyberAv3ngers) on Nov 9.

incidents.victim: Vanderbilt University
incidents.vector: Ransomware gang BYOD gained access to campus IT systems and devices, prompting the university to tell students and staff to shut down devices and disconnect from campus WiFi.
incidents.impact: The BYOD ransomware group added Vanderbilt to its dark web leak site and claims to have stolen data; the university's IT team is actively investigating and containing the incident.

incidents.victim: Mittwald CM Service (German web hosting provider)
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a flaw in Mittwald's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, used to connect customer AI assistants to its mStudio hosting platform, to gain unauthorized access.
incidents.impact: Hackers compromised 56 customer projects and evaded detection for eight days; Mittwald says the attacker's speed suggests AI-tool involvement, and it has engaged forensic experts and notified authorities.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian manufacturing company with a role in the transportation sector
incidents.vector: Belarusian government-linked hackers (tracked as FrostyNeighbor/GhostWriter) deployed destructive wiper malware against the victim's network.
incidents.impact: ESET reports this is the group's first-ever destructive data-wiping attack, marking an operational escalation from its usual espionage and influence activity.

incidents.victim: Hospitals, banks, financial companies, and a pet food company
incidents.vector: Three men used AI deepfake technology to impersonate corporate executives and lawyers in order to hijack and redirect business payments.
incidents.impact: The scheme defrauded companies of $129 million; two suspects were arrested in Spain and a third in the UK, all pending extradition to the US.

incidents.victim: 135 German citizens
incidents.vector: Scam call centers posing as financial advisers persuaded victims to invest in fraudulent cryptocurrency and stock platforms, then gained access to victims' crypto and banking accounts.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian police arrested four suspects, including the alleged leader, after the group stole more than €4.3 million ($4.8 million) from German victims.

incidents.victim: Maersk (Danish logistics giant) — claimed, unconfirmed
incidents.vector: A newly emerged ransomware and extortion group, WhiteArmor, claims to have breached Maersk's logistics platform.
incidents.impact: The group claims to have stolen 10GB of data, including driver records, staff accounts, and delivery receipts, and is demanding a $5 million Bitcoin payment; Maersk has not acknowledged the incident.

incidents.victim: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani and 17 other EU officials, law enforcement leaders, and journalists
incidents.vector: Pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16) published victims' personal data on a dark web portal and is offering cryptocurrency rewards for additional personal information.
incidents.impact: The campaign, seen as retaliation for a 2025 law enforcement takedown of the group's DDoS infrastructure, exposed officials' phone numbers, addresses, and family details, prompting G7 discussion of joint countermeasures.

incidents.victim: Rosstat (Russian Federal State Statistics Service)
incidents.vector: The Belarusian Cyber-Partisans hacktivist group breached Rosstat's systems.
incidents.impact: Russia's statistics agency has struggled to restore systems, delaying major economic data releases through at least Nov 13, with some previously published data missing from its website.

incidents.victim: Financial sector organizations in Southeast Asia and additional large financial firms globally
incidents.vector: Cambodia-based threat actor Storm-3358 used the agentic AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX combined with conventional tools to scan for and exploit flaws like anonymous file upload and SSRF, then installed open-source RATs (WISP, vshell, AdaptixC2) for persistence.
incidents.impact: Microsoft observed the group using AI agents for brute-forcing, password spraying, API abuse, and database dumping against financial organizations, accelerating lateral movement and data exfiltration.

incidents.victim: Li Auto EV owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers took over master user accounts of Li Auto smart EVs sold in Russia, many registered via Chinese eSIMs provided by importers, locking owners out of their vehicles.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed owners had their cars hijacked and were extorted to regain control, with the actual number of affected vehicles believed to be much higher.

incidents.victim: Binance
incidents.vector: North Korean operatives (tracked by the FBI as TraderTraitor) breached Binance and stole tokens across 11 different cryptocurrencies.
incidents.impact: The theft totaled $6.3 billion, the largest cryptocurrency heist in history; Binance was able to freeze about $2.8 billion in stablecoins, leaving roughly $3.25 billion in unrecoverable Bitcoin and Ethereum.

incidents.victim: A Ukrainian government entity
incidents.vector: A Belarus-nexus adversary exploited a modified CopyFail Linux privilege-escalation exploit to escalate from the web user www-data to root on a cPanel/WHM server, chaining it with the cPanel authentication-bypass zero-day (CVE-2026-41940).
incidents.impact: The adversary deployed a MythicC2 Poseidon agent, which CrowdStrike's Falcon sensor terminated before further compromise; the underlying cPanel vulnerability was later exploited at scale worldwide after public disclosure in late April 2026.

incidents.victim: Doctor Anywhere (Singapore telemedicine provider)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Doctor Anywhere's systems; the company has not disclosed the attack method.
incidents.impact: Stolen patient data includes full names, email addresses, ID and passport numbers, dates of birth, emergency contacts, and bank account details.

incidents.victim: Executive Office of the President (White House network)
incidents.vector: Residential proxy software — including Infatica, founded by a Russian national whose hosting firm was previously tied to 2016 election-system intrusions — was found running on White House staffer devices, likely bundled into free consumer apps, making the network's IP addresses available for rent to any paying customer.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed 236 proxy exits from the White House's dedicated network over a 30-day period via 28 separate residential proxy services, creating a channel that could be abused for anonymized malicious traffic or network reconnaissance.

incidents.victim: Consumers globally — 1.3 million+ Android TV boxes and 10 million+ other IoT devices
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ad fraud / proxy network
incidents.vector: Chinese manufacturer Videostrong Technology Co. intentionally built a backdoor into Android TV set-top boxes (and other IoT devices) that enrolled them in a botnet and installed residential-proxy and ad-fraud software without user consent.
incidents.impact: Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE botnet, severing access to over 1.3 million confirmed devices and an estimated 10 million+ additional compromised IoT devices, including telehealth devices and digital signage.

incidents.victim: Foreign ministries, defense/pharmaceutical/semiconductor/nuclear/financial firms, and telecom providers across 14+ countries
incidents.vector: The actor used the agentic AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX, paired with the DeepSeek LLM, to run fully automated intrusions in parallel, chaining vulnerabilities like SAML/XXE flaws and abusing cloud metadata services, at speeds exceeding 1,500 commands per hour.
incidents.impact: More than 200 organizations were targeted since Oct 17, with roughly 140 (about 70%) confirmed or suspected compromised within 11 days, including foreign ministries, a European presidency and prime minister's office, and 19 US organizations in sensitive sectors; the campaign remains active.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure — telecom, government, defense contractors, water, energy, transportation, maritime, rail, aviation, and emergency services organizations
incidents.vector: The group continuously rebuilds ephemeral chains of compromised SOHO routers, IoT devices, and enterprise edge infrastructure (from vendors including Fortinet, Cisco, Ivanti, F5, and Palo Alto Networks) — rebuildable in under two minutes — to mask the origin of intrusions and preserve long-term access, including zero-day exploitation of centralized management platforms.
incidents.impact: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs has notified hundreds of victims of this 'Silent Train' covert access framework, which has been active since late 2023 and systematically targets strategically valuable US networks.

incidents.victim: Space/satellite services, defense/aerospace technology, and policy research organizations
incidents.vector: UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass vulnerability in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances, then deployed the custom KeyDrift malware framework to intercept decrypted control-plane traffic from inside legitimate controller processes.
incidents.impact: Talos assesses the actor's infrastructure overlaps considerably with Volt Typhoon's 'Silent Train' network, enabling long-term persistent access and automated exfiltration of sensitive SD-WAN encryption key material.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Homeland Security
incidents.vector: A hacktivist group calling itself Department of Peace breached an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS and extracted internal personnel data; Okta says it found no evidence its own systems were compromised.
incidents.impact: Data on more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors, including officials overseeing covert operations and immigration enforcement, was published on a now-offline leak site in what the hacktivists described as retaliation for increased ICE operations.

incidents.victim: U.S. and allied businesses that unknowingly employ DPRK IT workers
incidents.vector: DPRK IT workers use fraudulent documents, stolen identities, and AI tools to secure remote employment at Western companies, then launder wages through cryptocurrency and, in some cases, exploit their network access to deploy malware and exfiltrate proprietary data.
incidents.impact: Treasury's OFAC sanctioned 10 individuals and a facilitator entity (FFTDC) for moving illicit proceeds — tens of millions of dollars funding North Korea's weapons programs — through Russia-based IT worker delegations.

incidents.victim: Government of Moldova
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Moldovan government networks and began extracting data before IT staff detected the intrusion.
incidents.impact: Officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach, which exposed the personal information of roughly one-third of Moldova's population — one of the country's worst cybersecurity incidents.

incidents.victim: Government and commercial websites running PHP (Europe and worldwide); Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS customers with exposed management interfaces
incidents.vector: Two critical PHP remote-code-execution flaws (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, dubbed PHP2Shell) let attackers trigger out-of-memory and use-after-free conditions via longjmp() error handling to achieve arbitrary code execution; one campaign chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug to gain root on PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Government websites across Europe went offline on disclosure day; Palo Alto Networks confirmed active exploitation against the small fraction (~0.02%) of its customers with internet-exposed management interfaces, and over 22 million potentially vulnerable internet-facing instances were identified globally.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime, and global sea shipping companies
incidents.vector: Ransomware and extortion group n0n compromised a maritime IT services provider and pivoted through the supply chain to reach its downstream port and shipping company customers, many of whom use CyberLogitec's IT platforms.
incidents.impact: All victims were listed on n0n's dark web leak site on Oct 12, with payment deadlines expiring a week later; roughly half of the listed companies are known CyberLogitec customers.

incidents.victim: Federal Bureau of Investigation (fbijobs.gov)
incidents.vector: Hackers aligned with the ShinyHunters extortion group breached the FBI's recruitment website, fbijobs.gov.
incidents.impact: Stolen files reportedly included employee medical and psychological records, Social Security numbers, home addresses, and unit/specialization details; investigators also identified ransom-negotiation firm executives who allegedly maintained close ties to the extortion group.
